gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the portable speakers' headline battery claims are measured at 50% volume. The soundcore Boom Go 3i's 24 h also requires the lights off: soundcore's own figures fall to 12 h with the lights on at 50% volume and to 6 h at 100% volume. Tribit's 24 h for the StormBox Micro 3 is measured at 50% volume with default EQ. Avantree's Roadtrip music time is 8 h at 60% volume. In a car, road noise pushes the volume up, so the claims on the shelf are not comparable.
standout_why: I read itechguides.com (rank 2). It gives Avantree Roadtrip as 12 h talk / 8 h music at 60% volume, and its CK11, Besign BK06 and VeoPulse figures carry no volume condition. It says nothing about the portable speakers ChatGPT recommended (JBL Clip 5) or that our page lists (Tribit StormBox Micro 3, soundcore Boom Go 3i). It also flags without explanation that the Roadtrip's title claims 22 h and 6 W while the body text says dual 3 W. dashanddrive.com would not open (certificate error) and avantree.com returned HTTP 429, so I could not check them. No rival page I read puts the 50%-volume condition, the lights-on/off split or a full-volume runtime next to each claim. Our current page already shows 'Boom Go 3i 24 h (6 h at full volume)', so the new part is the matched 50%-volume basis across brands plus the lights-on 12 h figure.
decides: On a matched basis (50% volume, default sound settings) the Tribit StormBox Micro 3 (24 h) and Boom Go 3i (24 h, lights off) tie. With its lights on, the Boom Go 3i gives half that (12 h), and it drops to 6 h at full volume, which is likely in a noisy cabin. This supports the Tribit as the 'no radio' pick: same claimed runtime, a built-in mic for hands-free calls (the Boom Go 3i has none per our table), and Tribit calls its 13 W the 'sustained working power'. The battery column should be footnoted '@50% volume' and show the Boom Go 3i as '24 h lights off / 12 h lights on / 6 h max'.
